title: Golden-Mars Transmission Project Decision Trail — Phase 65 Northern Virginia large-load delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Northern Virginia large-load delivery reporting pack. The SCC's Golden-Mars project decision advances a named transmission project while the preferred route remains contingent on a Loudoun County School Board land decision and an alternate route remains available.
key_findings: The state regulatory decision authorizes a named transmission project.
The preferred route still depends on a separate local land decision, with an alternate route preserved.
Land control, final engineering, rights of way, construction, energization, and customer service remain downstream.
why_it_matters: Which records connect load forecasts, local land-use rules, utility decisions, transmission, environmental permits, water, service acceptance, and reliability? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The record is a concrete example of how state authorization and local control interlock before grid capacity can be delivered.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a named project trail to the Northern Virginia corridor.
Separates approval, route resolution, build, energization, and service.
Supports later monitoring of a high-value conversion bottleneck.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The official link is a commission information rail; project claims should remain tied to the underlying case record.
Approval does not establish final land control or a built route.
No delivered customer capacity or service should be inferred.
